cicchakti
(‘sentient power’)
------------------------------------------
The भक्ति schools of Vedānta as those propounded by निम्बार्क (14th cent. A. D.), वल्लभ (A.

-1533) and श्रीकण्ठ (13th cent. A. D.) have tried to reconcile the existence side by side, of the cit or conscious and the अचित् or unconscious aspects of च्रेअतिओन् within the broad framework of advaita or non-dualism. According to these schools, ब्रह्मन्, the Absolute or God, has two aspects of power: cit-शक्ति (also चिच्छक्ति) or the sentient power and the अचित्-शक्ति (also अचिच्छक्ति) or the insentient power.
God in his own nature, is absolutely formless pure चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स्. By चिच्छक्ति or the sentient power he holds the individual souls within him. By अचिच्छक्ति or the insentient power he spreads out the material world and connects it with the former for their diverse experiences.
Cicchakti (sometimes called ‘svarūpa-śākti’ or ‘antaraṅgaśakti’) again, is said to have three aspects—sandhinī, saṁvit and hlādinī—corresponding respectively to the sat, cit and आनन्द aspects of God. By sandhinī God upholds his own existence and that of others. By saṁvit he knows and makes others know. By ह्लादिनी, he enjoys and makes others enjoy bliss.
See also ACICCHAKTI.
